episodes.204292: A complex of showers and thunderstorms dropped southeats into northeast and north central Alabama during the early morning hours. Isolated flash flooding was reported in Jackson County. Additional clusters of thunderstorms developed during the midday into the afternoon across northwest Alabama. One of these thunderstorms knocked down a tree in Lauderdale County.
episodes.204293: Isolated flash flooding in southern middle Tennessee.
episodes.204310: Surface cold front stationed west of the region allowed for ample heating across the Susquehanna Valley during the afternoon and evening hours of August 13, 2025. Marginal shear and ample instability allowed for convection to begin firing, with strong-to-marginally severe thunderstorms to occur across southeastern Pennsylvania. An isolated instance of tree damage was observed in Lancaster County. Precipitable water values ranging generally between 1.50 and 2.00 allowed for efficient rainfall in thunderstorms across York and Lancaster Counties, with a basement taking on water in southern York County.
episodes.204381: A cold front swept through southern New England in the afternoon bringing a line of storms, a few of which were severe. These caused sporadic wind damage and some limited flash flooding in northeast MA.
episodes.204382: A cold front swept through southern New England in the afternoon bringing a line of storms, a few of which were severe. These caused sporadic wind damage and some limited flash flooding in northeast MA.
episodes.204463: An eastward progression of an upper ridge brought southerly flow to Nevada, leading to an increase in moisture and instability. This resulted in afternoon showers and thunderstorms that produced heavy rain and  strong outflow winds.
episodes.204684: Slow moving thunderstorms along a frontal boundary resulted in a localized two to four inches of rain. This resulted in instances of flash flooding.
episodes.204685: Slow moving thunderstorms along a frontal boundary resulted in a localized two to four inches of rain. This resulted in instances of flash flooding.
episodes.204737: An isolated severe thunderstorm produced localized wind damage in the City of Charlottesville.
episodes.204739: A couple of thunderstorms produced localized gale-force wind gusts over the middle tidal Potomac River and the upper Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.204914: Scattered showers and thunderstorms blossomed across the area on the 13th of August as a cold front slowly approached from the northwest. The front eventually reached the Ohio River around midnight and then proceeded southeast through West Virginia by the afternoon of the 14th. ||In addition to producing heavy downpours, thunderstorms began training across portions of southeast Ohio and southwest West Virginia during this timeframe. These heavy showers and storms produced one to two inches of rain across much of northeastern West Virginia, with pockets of two to four inches prompting some flash flooding in Wood, Wirt, and Roane Counties during the afternoon and evening. Down towards the I-64 corridor, training storms produced a swath of two to five inch rainfall amounts across portions of Cabell County, which resulted in street flooding in Huntington during the night. Flooding came to an end as precipitation shifted south and then tapered off before daybreak on the 14th.
episodes.205174: Scattered thunderstorms resulted in a couple of measured wind gusts in excess of 34 knots.
episodes.205361: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the evening hours ahead of a frontal boundary moving through the Ohio Valley.
episodes.205640: A weak upper low helped advect near record moisture into Tennessee, where a boundary and classic heavy rain profiles combined to produce extreme rainfall rates over portions of Chattanooga, leading to numerous water rescues, a few evacuations, flooded interstate and local roads, flooded homes, and unfortunately a few fatalities. One fatality occurred in the east Brainerd area after a driver went around police barricades and was swept away in the flood waters. Damage estimates as of September 2025 were at least $1.7 million dollars per emergency management.
episodes.205692: A moist airmass and a good deal of instability during the afternoon triggered scattered severe thunderstorms. These storms produced damaging wind gusts north of M-59.
episodes.205735: A thunderstorm moving through the Detroit River produced a wind gust just under 35 knots.
episodes.205892: Southwest steering flow over a moist and unstable airmass triggered scattered strong storms along the inland progressing west and east coast sea breezes. The sea breezes and outflows merged toward the eastern side of the state where a few strong to pulses severe storms with wind damage occurred.
episodes.205893: Southwest steering flow over a moist and unstable airmass triggered scattered strong storms along the inland progressing west and east coast sea breezes. The sea breezes and outflows merged toward the eastern side of the state where a few strong to pulses severe storms with wind damage occurred.
episodes.206323: Multiple rounds of showers and thunderstorms overnight, culminated with some particularly heavy rain on the morning of August 13th in both Knox and Sullivan counties. This resulted in some flash flooding in both areas.
episodes.206506: Severe thunderstorm outflow winds occurred in parts of extreme southeast Idaho.
episodes.206513: Isolated thunderstorms developed over the northern Nebraska Panhandle and southwestern South Dakota during the early evening hours of August 13th. This activity became better organized as a bow echo as it tracked east across far northern Nebraska into the evening hours. This activity eventually exited Wheeler and Holt counties after 2 AM CDT on August 14th. Hail up to golf ball size and thunderstorm wind gusts up to 65 MPH were reported with the strongest storms.
episodes.206552: A cold front with strong shortwave energy moved into a hot, humid, and unstable airmass, triggering the development thunderstorms in eastern Pennsylvania. These storms produced frequent lightning with damage from a lightning strike reported.
episodes.206553: A cold front with strong shortwave energy moved into a hot, humid, and unstable airmass, triggering the development of strong to severe thunderstorms in New Jersey. These storms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.206611: Showers and thunderstorms developed ahead of a prefrontal trough and again along lake and residual outflow boundaries. With PWAT values near 2.00 inches, some storms did produce efficient rainfall for flash flooding.
episodes.206635: A pre-frontal trough, or elongated area of low pressure, was responsible for thunderstorms and subsequent flash flooding.
episodes.206636: A pre-frontal trough, or elongated area of low pressure, was responsible for thunderstorms and subsequent flash flooding.
episodes.206668: Weak southwest flow aloft, ahead of an approaching upper-level trough, induced low-level moisture return across southern Illinois through the day. By late afternoon, surface-based CAPE was around 3000 J/kg and downdraft CAPE was 800-1000 J/kg. With weak flow aloft, the shear was also weak. In the early evening an isolated storm produced a significant downburst as it moved east northeast across Grayville.
episodes.206669: Weak southwest flow aloft, ahead of an approaching upper-level trough, induced low-level moisture return across southwest Indiana through the day. By late afternoon, surface-based CAPE was around 3000 J/kg and downdraft CAPE was 800-1000 J/kg. With weak flow aloft, the shear was also weak. One isolated storm produced a downburst as it moved north across Spencer County during the late afternoon. In the evening, a small cluster of storms produced sporadic wind damage as it moved east northeast from northern Gibson County into northern Pike County.
episodes.206670: Scattered showers and thunderstorms formed in Southern Illinois during the afternoon of the 13th in the vicinity of a cold front as a weak shortwave trough was draped across the area. One of these showers produced a cold air funnel near Tamaroa. The environment had decent low-level moisture with drier mid-levels.
episodes.206699: An upper-level trough situated over Texas and the Southern Plains created a series of showers and storms across North Texas during the overnight hours of August 11th into August 12th, and again on the morning of August 13th. Significant rainfall from a few of these storms resulted in localized flooding.
episodes.206700: Thunderstorms developed during the late afternoon of the 13th in the warm humid airmass in advance of an approaching cold front. Small scale downbursts associated with  isolated collapsing pulse type thunderstorms produced localized damaging wind gusts. The wind gusts toppled and/or snapped trees at several locations.
episodes.206713: Hot and humid conditions ahead of an upper level disturbance and surface boundary generated enough instability to drive the development of scattered thunderstorms across northwest Connecticut on the afternoon of August 13, 2025.  One storm in particular reached severe magnitude, inflicting wind damage to wires near Sharon which ended up causing a brush fire on Cornwall Bridge Road.
episodes.206714: Hot and humid conditions ahead of an upper level disturbance and surface boundary generated enough instability to drive the development of scattered thunderstorms across eastern New York on the afternoon of August 13, 2025.  A cluster of storms reached severe magnitudes, inflicting tree and wire damage in Schoharie, Albany, and Greene Counties that lead to several road closures and subsequent traffic delays. Some of the roadways impacted include Harpersfield Road, Blodgett Hill Road, and Route 81. Damage to a car was additionally reported due to downed wires near Route 143 and Waterboard Road near Coeymans Hollow.
episodes.206715: Hot and humid conditions ahead of an upper level disturbance and surface boundary generated enough instability to drive the development of scattered thunderstorms across southern Vermont on the afternoon of August 13, 2025.  One storm in particular reached severe magnitude, inflicting wind damage to trees and wires along North Road at Beacon Hollow Road and Sunderland Hill Road near Arlington.
episodes.206728: During the overnight and early morning hours of August 12th and 13th, strong thunderstorms associated with a trough tracking through the area crossed Lake Erie, resulting in gusty winds to at least 34 knots across portions of the lake. As the thunderstorms continued across the lake and onshore, they weakened some, remaining below marine/land based warning criteria.
episodes.206735: A weak upper trough extending southwest to northeast across the area triggered slow moving thunderstorms in El Paso which led to flash flooding on the west side.
episodes.206751: Two clusters of storms would move across the forecast area on the 13th into the early morning hours of the 14th. The day started with an isolated stronger storm generating 1 inch hail 6 miles north northeast of Lowry. That cluster would continue to move east and intensify, with 1.5 inch hail observed 8 miles east of Pierpont. These storms would damage siding and crops around Pierpont, with additional thunderstorm wind damage to trees in the town of Roslyn. ||Another cluster of storms would move through central South Dakota, with a peak wind gust of 73 mph recorded by the South Dakota State University mesonet station 12 miles south of Vivian. As this cluster departed and weakened, additional winds were generated, with a gust of 68 mph 3 miles southeast of Reliance on a South Dakota Department of Transportation mesonet station.||A total of 3.6 inches was observed 6 miles east southeast of Pierpont. This rainfall, on top of already saturated soils from the previous month's heavy rains, resulted in water over roads, a partial washout, and at least one stranded vehicle in this area. In Roslyn, a trained spotter recorded 4.64 inches.
episodes.206774: Heavy rain caused flooding in Baldwin County.
episodes.206908: A moderately unstable airmass with deep moisture and warm temperatures led to an environment supportive of thunderstorms producing damaging wind gusts across coastal waters.
episodes.207028: A weak area of low pressure moved into Northeastern Pennsylvania during the afternoon which provided a focus for heavy rain-producing thunderstorms. Several storms moved through the Wilkes-Barre and Scranton metro areas during the afternoon causing significant urban flash flooding of poor drainage and storm drain systems. Many roads were flooded in the area with several reports of stranded vehicles in the area.
episodes.207045: Although shear was overall weak, lift from an approaching pre-frontal trough and upper level trough combined with 1000-2000 J/kg of MLCAPE was enough for a few severe thunderstorms to develop and produce damaging wind gusts.
episodes.207047: Although shear was overall weak, lift from an approaching pre-frontal trough and upper level trough combined with 1000-2000 J/kg of MLCAPE was enough for a few severe thunderstorms to develop and produce damaging wind gusts.

episodes.207104: Mid-level atmospheric moisture moved over Wyoming causing scattered high-based showers and thunderstorms to develop. With dew point depressions greater than 50 degrees, wind gusts of 50 knots or higher were reported in portions of Johnson, Natrona, Sublette, and Sweetwater Counties.
episodes.207157: The region was experiencing well above normal temperatures, with high temperatures reaching the low to mid-90s. This created a very warm, humid, and unstable atmosphere. A pre-frontal surface trough moved into NH on the afternoon of August 13th, triggering numerous thunderstorms, a few of the storms became severe in nature.  In addition, very heavy rain fell in Nashua area, causing some minor urban flooding.
episodes.207166: Heavy rain caused Rio Guanajibo to overflow and flood PR-103 in Cabo Rojo.
episodes.207184: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed across portions of Mississippi during the afternoon and evening hours of August 13th through 17th. Isolated damaging wind gusts occurred with the strongest of storms.
episodes.207193: A squall line developed during and brought severe wind gusts across western SD.
episodes.207194: Cluster of severe thunderstorms brings severe damaging wind gusts to eastern Wyoming.
episodes.207208: Thunderstorms moved across New Haven County, CT producing 1 inch of rainfall an hour. A total of 4 to 5 inches fell across New Haven.
episodes.207210: Thunderstorm moved across northeast New Jersey resulting in a water rescue across Hudson County, cars stuck in flood waters across Essex County and Road closures across Union County.
episodes.207212: Thunderstorms moved across Jamaica, Queens resulting in flooding and road closures.
episodes.207232: A typical summertime pattern was in place across the region, with intense daytime heating and abundant low-level moisture leading to the development of numerous afternoon thunderstorms. The storms were primarily outflow-driven, producing locally strong and gusty winds. One storm produce a microburst that downed a few trees in Woodland View Estates in Central/Greenwell Springs.
episodes.207314: High-based thunderstorms coming off the Beartooths produced winds gusting up to 60 mph.
episodes.208193: Hot and humid weather continued ahead of a cold front marching across the Upper Great Lakes late in the day. A line of thunderstorms crossed the UP during the evening hours with this cold front, resulting in some gusty winds.
